searchText: the code hash is the Keccack of the code, so _not_ 32x0. Empty accounts have an assigned code size, according to the spec. storage value are taken from the EVM and stored as is, so they are big endian because that's what the EVM does. Nonce, balance and code size are little endian. Okay thank you Is there some specs about value formatting? Anyway Btw, Pedersen state was generated in 13 hours with 120 GB of Disk footprint but I can do better, lots of leading 0s and lots of re-encryption and repetion of keys everything is a 32-byte value that's pretty good (for the time it took, that is)! iirc, geth was taking roughly 18h if we discounted the preimage problem, so it's the correct order of magnitude one last question: If we have a self destructed code, what do we do with it? we insert it in the Tree or we keep it out? and what about the storage slots associated with it Nevermind, I managed to get the answer to my question
